newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to list state-owned JR Tokai shares in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Japan to list state-owned JR Tokai shares in Oct.

text.p: Japan on Tuesday announced that it will sell most of its shares in the formerly state-run Central Japan Railway Co (JR Tokai), as it seeks to shore up the government's debt-ridden finances.
Analysts warned, however, that the October 8 listing could hurt the stock market by adding to a glut of shares, especially if the government sells shares in other formerly state-owned firms as well.

"JR Tokai shares will pull funds out of the market, funds which were meant for other stocks," said a general manager at a medium-sized Japanese brokerage. "This is definitely bad news for the market and the index."

JR Tokai, one of six passenger railway operators formed by the 1987 breakup and privatisation of the government's debt-ridden Japanese National Railways (JNR), will be the third JR firm to be listed on Japan's stock exchanges.
Of the 1.5 million JR Tokai shares to be listed on Japanese bourses, 700,000 will be auctioned and the rest will be sold through a secondary offering. At present, JR Tokai shares number 2.24 million.
On June 30, JR Tokai formally applied for its shares to be listed on the Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya and Kyoto bourses.
Snowballing national debt left over from the former JNR has posed a big headache for the government, which is struggling to put its fiscal house in order.

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Saturday that the Japanese people will have to foot the bill for 23 trillion yen ($201 billion) in debt still left from the privatisation of JNR 10 years ago, equivalent to 200,000 yen ($1,754) per citizen.

He said that of the 28 trillion yen ($245 billion) in remaining JNR debt, five trillion yen ($43.8 billion) will be covered by selling off state-owned land and stock holdings. The remaining 23 trillion yen ($201 billion) must come either from existing government funds or from a new tax, he said.

The planned listing of JR Tokai shares could pave the way for sales of other state-owned shares in Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and East Japan Railway Co (JR East), adding to concerns about an oversupply of shares in the market, analysts said.
Analysts said their evaluation of JR Tokai shares fell behind that of JR East and West Japan Railway Co (JR West), both of which are already traded on Japanese bourses.
JR Tokai's profitability depends heavily on a bullet train service used by 100,000 passengers a day, which some analysts said is potentially risky.
On the Tokyo bourse, JR West shares fell 16,000 yen to close at 426,000 on Tuesday, while JR East added 4,000 yen to 579,000 yen. ($1=114 yen)
